questions.stem: A 2-month pregnant female presented with Plasmodium vivax malaria. Which of the following is the appropriate treatment for this patient? (Fmge Jan 2024)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Quinine

 

For a pregnant woman with Plasmodium vivax malaria, Chloroquine alone is the appropriate choice. Primaquine is contraindicated during pregnancy due to potential risks to the fetus. Quinine is normally used for Plasmodium falciparum malaria but can be used in P. vivax malaria also if other options are not available. It is safe in pregnancy. ACTs are generally avoided in the first trimester, and Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy. Therefore, Chloroquine, without Primaquine, is the safest and most effective option in this case. However, as it is not in the options, so the next best option i.e. quinine will be the answer.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Chloroquine plus Primaquine: Chloroquine is considered safe and effective for the treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria during pregnancy. However, primaquine is contraindicated in pregnancy due to the risk of hemolytic anemia in the fetus, especially if there is G6PD deficiency, which cannot be tested for in the fetus.

 

Option C. Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT): While ACTs are very effective in treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria, their safety profile in the first trimester of pregnancy is not well-established. Generally, they are avoided in the first trimester unless no other options are available.

 

Option D. Doxycycline: Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy due to the risk of interfering with bone and teeth development in the fetus.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Quinine is often used as a treatment for malaria during pregnancy, especially if other options are not available or suitable. However, it is usually more associated with the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum rather than Plasmodium vivax.

However, it is usually more associated with the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum rather than Plasmodium vivax.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the mechanism of action of amloride?

options.label: A
options.text: Blockade of Na-Cl symporter in DCT

options.label: B
options.text: Blockade of Na K 2Cl symporter in Loop of Henle

options.label: C
options.text: Blockade of aldosterone receptors in collecting duct

options.label: D
options.text: Blockade of epithelial sodium channels in collecting duct

questions.answerText: Blockade of epithelial sodium channels in collecting duct
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Blockade of epithelial sodium channels in the collecting duct

 

  • Amiloride is a potassium-sparing diuretic that acts by blocking epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) in the collecting duct of the nephron.
  • This prevents sodium reabsorption, reducing potassium and hydrogen ion excretion, which helps in preventing hypokalemia.
  • It is commonly used in combination with thiazide or loop diuretics to counteract potassium loss.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Blockade of Na-Cl symporter in DCT: Incorrect

 

  • This is the mechanism of thiazide diuretics (e.g., Hydrochlorothiazide, Chlorthalidone).
  • They work in the distal convoluted tubule (DCT) and promote sodium and water excretion.

 

Option B. Blockade of Na-K-2Cl symporter in Loop of Henle: Incorrect

 

  • This is the mechanism of loop diuretics (e.g., Furosemide, Bumetanide, Torsemide).
  • They inhibit the Na-K-2Cl symporter in the thick ascending limb, leading to potent diuresis.

 

Option C. Blockade of aldosterone receptors in the collecting duct: Incorrect

 

  • This is the mechanism of aldosterone antagonists like Spironolactone and Eplerenone.
  • They inhibit aldosterone's action, reducing sodium reabsorption and increasing potassium retention.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • Amiloride blocks ENaC in the collecting duct → potassium-sparing diuretic
  • Used to counteract hypokalemia from thiazide or loop diuretics
  • Thiazides block Na-Cl symporter in DCT, loop diuretics block Na-K-2Cl symporter in Henle
  • Aldosterone antagonists block aldosterone receptors, not ENaC directly

questions.stem: A 53-year-old male presented with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Which of the following anti-diabetic drug acts by causing glucosuria? (Fmge Jan 2024)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Empagliflozin

 

Empagliflozin, as an SGLT2 inhibitor, is the drug among the options provided that acts specifically by causing glucosuria. This mechanism is unique to SGLT2 inhibitors and is a direct way of lowering blood glucose levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus. The other drugs listed work through different mechanisms that do not involve the induction of glucosuria.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Acarbose: This drug is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor. It works by slowing down the digestion of carbohydrates in the intestine, thereby reducing the rise in blood glucose after meals. It does not cause glucosuria.

 

Option B. Glipizide: Glipizide is a sulfonylurea. It works by stimulating insulin release from the pancreatic beta cells. It does not cause glucosuria.

 

Option D. Sitagliptin: Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor. It works by increasing the levels of incretin hormones, which increase insulin release and decrease glucagon release in a glucose-dependent manner. It does not cause glucosuria.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Empagliflozin is an SGLT2 (Sodium-Glucose Co-Transporter-2) inhibitor, works by blocking glucose reabsorption in the kidney, leading to increased glucose excretion in the urine, i.e., glucosuria.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child with a previous history of GTCS presents with convulsions which are ongoing since 25 minutes. What should be the appropriate immediate management of this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) Lorazepam

 

The child is experiencing status epilepticus (SE), defined as a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes or recurrent seizures without regaining consciousness for ≥30 minutes. Immediate treatment is required to prevent neuronal damage and complications.

 

  • First-line drug: Benzodiazepines (Lorazepam, Diazepam, or Midazolam)
    • Lorazepam (IV) is preferred due to longer duration of action and fewer respiratory depressant effects.
    • If IV access is unavailable, intramuscular (IM) Midazolam or rectal Diazepam can be used.
  • Second-line drugs (if seizures persist after 2 doses of benzodiazepines):
    • IV Valproate, IV Phenytoin/Fosphenytoin, or IV Levetiracetam
  • Refractory status epilepticus (if seizures persist >30-60 min despite treatment):
    • Requires general anesthesia (propofol, midazolam, or thiopental infusion) in ICU.

 

Other Options:

 

Option B. Valproate: Incorrect

 

  • Valproate is used for seizure control, but not as first-line in acute status epilepticus.
  • It is a second-line option if benzodiazepines fail.

 

Option C. Ethosuximide: Incorrect

 

  • Ethosuximide is used for absence seizures (petit mal), not generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS) or status epilepticus.

 

Option D. Carbamazepine: Incorrect

 

  • Carbamazepine is used for focal (partial) seizures, not for status epilepticus.
  • It can worsen generalized seizures like GTCS.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the preferred drug for treatment of post-menopausal breast cancer? (Fmge Jan 2024)
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Anastrozole

 

Aromatase inhibitors like anastrozole and letrozole are  considered the preferred drugs for the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in post-menopausal women whereas tamoxifen is considered drug of choice in pre-menopausal women. Anastrozole is an aromatase inhibitor whereas tamoxifen works as a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), both are effective in blocking the effects of estrogen on breast cancer cells. Methotrexate may be used in breast cancer treatment, however it is not a first line drug. On the other hand, raloxifene is a SERM used for treatment of osteoporosis

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Methotrexate: Methotrexate is a chemotherapy drug used in the treatment of various cancers, including some types of breast cancer. However, it is not typically the first-line choice for post-menopausal breast cancer.

 

Option B. Raloxifene: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) primarily used for osteoporosis and the prevention of breast cancer, rather than its treatment.

 

Option C. Tamoxifen: Tamoxifen is a widely used medication for the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in both pre-menopausal and post-menopausal women. It is often the preferred choice for breast cancer in pre-menopausal female.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Anastrozole is an aromatase inhibitor and is drug of choice for treatment of breast cancer (which is estrogen receptor positive) in post-menopausal females.

questions.stem: A patient with history of HIV was started on anti-retroviral therapy consisting of lamivudine 300 mg, tenofovir 150 mg and dolutegravir 50 mg once daily at night. Few weeks later, he developed tuberculosis and was started on anti-tubercular drugs. Which of the following dose adjustment may be required in this patient? (Fmge Jan 2024)

options.label: B
options.text: Add tenofovir 150 mg in the morning

options.label: C
options.text: Add lamivudine 300 mg in the morning

options.label: D
options.text: Add dolutegravir 50 mg in the morning

questions.answerText: Add dolutegravir 50 mg in the morning
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Add dolutegravir 50 mg in the morning

 

Adjustment of ARV regimen with concomitant ATT:

 

  • When a patient already on 2NRTIs + 1NNRTI (EFV)–based regimen has to be given 2HRZE + 4HRE–based ATT for the newly detected TB, same ART regimen can be continued without any modification.
  • When a patient already on 2NRTIs + DTG–based regimen has to be given Rifampicin-based ATT for the newly detected TB, same ART regimen can be continued. However, since co-administered rifampicin reduces bioavailability of DTG, which can be overcome by an additional tablet of DTG 50 mg (at an interval of 12 hours with the regular dose of DTG) till the completion of ATT. Once the ATT is completed, additional tablet of DTG 50 mg should be stopped 2 weeks after stoppage of Rifampicin-containing treatment regimen.
  • When a patient already on 2NRTIs + PI–based regimen develops TB, ART regimen has to be modified if 2HREZ + 4HRE–based ATT is co-administered.
    • If the patient has not taken DTG earlier, patient is shifted to 2 NRTIs + DLG-based regimen with twice daily DTG as discussed in last section
    • If DLG cannot be given due to any reason and boosted PIs need to continued, then rifampicin should be replaced by rifabutin

 

Educational Objective:

 

In patients on a dolutegravir-based regimen who start rifampicin-based anti-tubercular therapy, an additional dose of dolutegravir 50 mg should be taken in the morning (12 hours apart from the regular dose) to maintain effective drug levels and manage HIV effectively.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after ingesting an overdose of a medication. In order to enhance drug clearance, you consider the modification of urinary pH as a therapeutic measure. Knowing that manipulating the urinary pH can increase the excretion of certain drugs by altering their ionization state, which of the following drugs would not have its excretion increased by alkalinization of the urine?
questions.solutionHtml:
ng>Acidifying the urine would increase morphine excretion.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Aspirin: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is an acidic drug. Alkalinizing the urine with agents such as sodium bicarbonate can enhance its ionization and excretion.

 

Option B. Methotrexate: This is also an acidic drug, and alkalinization of the urine will increase its ionization, decreasing reabsorption and increasing elimination.

 

Option D. Phenobarbitone: This is an acidic drug, and like aspirin and methotrexate, it is more ionized in alkaline urine, leading to increased excretion.

 

Educational Objective:

 

In cases of drug overdose, urinary alkalinization is utilized to increase the excretion of acidic drugs by enhancing their ionization, which does not apply to basic drugs like morphine that are better excreted in acidic conditions. Remember, the drugs ending with ‘ine’ are basic.

questions.stem: A patient of Prinzmetal’s angina is started on isosorbide mono nitrate. What is the mechanism of action of nitrates in this condition?

options.label: B
options.text: Increased left ventricular end diastolic volume

questions.solutionHtml:
educing the contractility of the heart.

 

Option B. Increased left ventricular end diastolic volume: Incorrect because nitrates do not typically increase left ventricular end-diastolic volume; they reduce preload and afterload through vasodilation.

 

Option C. Decreased diastolic perfusion pressure: Incorrect as nitrates do not reduce diastolic perfusion pressure; their action is aimed at reducing vasospasm and increasing perfusion.

 

Educational objective:

 

In Prinzmetal’s angina, nitrates like isosorbide mononitrate work by causing endothelium independent coronary vasodilation, acting directly on the vascular smooth muscle through NO donation, which leads to pain relief by reversing the coronary vasospasm.
